notes: Replaced commit-sync-versus-async-waiting with synchronous-commit-wait-timeout to avoid an API-name giveaway. Replaced sync-commit-flushes-prior-async-commits with asynchronous-commit-callback-thread because the javadoc's sequencing wording differs between commit methods.

cards.statement: Kafka brokers push newly appended records to KafkaConsumer as they arrive.
cards.explanation: KafkaConsumer retrieves records by requesting them from brokers.
cards.misconception: Brokers initiate delivery when new records arrive.

cards.statement: max.poll.records limits how many records KafkaConsumer fetches in a single broker request.
cards.explanation: max.poll.records caps poll() results; fetched records remain cached.
cards.misconception: The poll limit also limits each broker fetch.

source.title: Kafka 4.3 Consumer and Share Consumer Configs

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer.wakeup() is safe to call from another thread during a blocked consumer operation.
cards.explanation: wakeup() is the exception to KafkaConsumer's thread-safety restriction.

cards.statement: Kafka assigns a subscribed partition to one consumer within a consumer group.
cards.explanation: Kafka divides consumption using partition ownership.

cards.statement: Consumers with different group.id values share the same consumption position for a partition.
cards.explanation: Different consumer groups track their consumption independently.
cards.misconception: Different groups share a common reading position.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer.assign() can enlist the group coordinator to distribute its selected partitions.
cards.explanation: Manually assigned consumers act independently.
cards.misconception: Manual assignment uses the group's partition coordination.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer.position() returns its most recently committed offset during active consumption.
cards.explanation: position() identifies the next record; recovery uses committed offsets.
cards.misconception: The current position is the durable restart position.

cards.statement: Kafka stores consumer group offset commits in its __consumer_offsets topic.
cards.explanation: The group coordinator appends offset commits to this internal topic.

cards.statement: With auto.offset.reset=latest, a consumer risks skipping records sent before discovery of a new partition.
cards.explanation: With auto.offset.reset=latest, the consumer starts at a new partition's end, skipping earlier records.

source.title: Kafka 4.3 Consumer and Share Consumer Configs

cards.statement: A call to KafkaConsumer.seek() with an earlier retained offset rewinds an assigned partition.
cards.explanation: KafkaConsumer.seek() changes an assigned partition's next read position.

cards.statement: Kafka preserves an empty group's committed offsets until the topic's record retention expires.
cards.explanation: An empty group's offsets expire according to offsets.retention.minutes.
cards.misconception: Topic data retention determines committed-offset retention.

cards.statement: Since Kafka 4.2, consumers in a share group acknowledge the delivery of individual records.
cards.explanation: Share groups track delivery completion at record granularity.
cards.volatilityNote: Share-group behavior continues to evolve across releases.

cards.statement: A successful KafkaProducer send confirms that a subscribing application's processing has completed.
cards.explanation: A producer acknowledgement concerns publication, not consumer processing.
cards.misconception: Producer success confirms downstream application processing.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer commits offsets periodically under its default configuration.
cards.explanation: enable.auto.commit defaults to true.

source.title: Kafka 4.3 Consumer and Share Consumer Configs

cards.statement: With auto commit, processing the full poll result before the next poll or close gives at-least-once delivery.
cards.explanation: Auto commit can advance past unfinished work at the next poll or close.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer can use max.poll.interval.ms to configure its commitSync() broker response timeout.
cards.explanation: The no-argument commitSync() bounds its wait using default.api.timeout.ms.
cards.misconception: The poll interval sets the synchronous commit timeout.

cards.statement: With enable.auto.commit=false, processing before commit prevents replay after a crash.
cards.explanation: A crash between processing and commit can cause the work to run again.
cards.misconception: Processing before committing prevents repeated processing.

cards.statement: A consumer can overwrite output by record primary key to make duplicate processing harmless.
cards.explanation: Repeated identical keyed overwrites preserve the stored output value.

cards.statement: With enable.auto.commit=false, a consumer can store output and offsets atomically in an external store.
cards.explanation: Atomically saving output with offsets ties a consumer's progress to its stored results.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer can return gaps in offsets on a transactional topic under either isolation level.
cards.explanation: Transaction markers occupy offsets but KafkaConsumer filters them from application records.

cards.statement: Kafka's default delivery guarantee gives an application exactly one processing attempt per record.
cards.explanation: Kafka defaults to at-least-once delivery.
cards.misconception: Kafka guarantees exactly-once processing by default.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer can invoke a later commitAsync() callback before an earlier call's callback.
cards.explanation: KafkaConsumer invokes commit callbacks in the order of their commit calls.
cards.misconception: Asynchronous commit callbacks can overtake earlier callbacks.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer runs OffsetCommitCallback on a dedicated thread separate from the poll loop.
cards.explanation: KafkaConsumer may execute the callback in a thread calling poll().
cards.misconception: Asynchronous commit callbacks run on a dedicated callback thread.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer.commitSync() can fail if a rebalance transfers partitions before the commit completes.
cards.explanation: The broker may reject a stale owner's commit with CommitFailedException.

cards.statement: A consumer joining a subscribed group can cause Kafka to redistribute its partitions.
cards.explanation: Group membership changes trigger Kafka's rebalance process.

cards.statement: A static member's exceeded max.poll.interval.ms lets Kafka reassign partitions before its session expires.
cards.explanation: Kafka waits for the static member's session timeout before reassignment.
cards.misconception: Static and dynamic members lose their partitions at the same poll deadline.

source.title: Kafka 4.3 Consumer and Share Consumer Configs

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer selects CooperativeStickyAssignor ahead of RangeAssignor in its default assignor list.
cards.explanation: RangeAssignor precedes CooperativeStickyAssignor in the default preference list.
cards.misconception: The default assignor list already prefers cooperative assignment.

source.title: Kafka 4.3 Consumer and Share Consumer Configs

cards.statement: RangeAssignor distributes partitions independently for subscribed topics.
cards.explanation: RangeAssignor balances each topic's partitions among its subscribers.

cards.statement: With CooperativeStickyAssignor, consumers keep ownership of their unmoved partitions throughout a rebalance.
cards.explanation: Consumers retain unchanged assignments while handing off partitions that move.

cards.statement: With group.protocol=classic, the consumer sets its failure-detection timeout through session.timeout.ms.
cards.explanation: The classic protocol uses the client's session.timeout.ms for failure detection.

source.title: Kafka 4.3 Consumer and Share Consumer Configs

cards.statement: Consumers sharing group.instance.id can remain active together in one group.
cards.explanation: Kafka fences duplicate static identities.
cards.misconception: Several active consumers can share the same static identity in a group.

cards.statement: ConsumerRebalanceListener exposes a callback for committing offsets before partition reassignment.
cards.explanation: An application can save offsets in onPartitionsRevoked() during a graceful handoff.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer selects group.protocol=consumer when the group.protocol setting is left unset.
cards.explanation: KafkaConsumer defaults to the classic group protocol in Kafka 4.3.
cards.misconception: Server availability of the consumer protocol makes it the client default.
cards.volatilityNote: The documented protocol timeline changes the KafkaConsumer default in a future release.

cards.statement: Since Kafka 4.0, group.protocol=consumer uses the client's partition.assignment.strategy for assignment.
cards.explanation: The broker assigns partitions; partition.assignment.strategy is unsupported.
cards.misconception: The consumer protocol retains the classic protocol's client-side assignor setting.

cards.statement: Since Kafka 4.0, with group.protocol=consumer, the broker controls the consumer heartbeat interval.
cards.explanation: For group.protocol=consumer, the broker sets group.consumer.heartbeat.interval.ms.

cards.statement: Since Kafka 4.0, KafkaConsumer evaluates SubscriptionPattern locally with group.protocol=consumer.
cards.explanation: The broker evaluates SubscriptionPattern expressions using the RE2J format.
cards.misconception: SubscriptionPattern matching runs in the consumer application.

cards.statement: KafkaProducer enables idempotence automatically when an application configures transactional.id.
cards.explanation: transactional.id implies enable.idempotence=true.

cards.statement: With transactional.id set, KafkaProducer can atomically commit records across several topics.
cards.explanation: One transaction spans its output partitions and topics.

cards.statement: KafkaProducer.sendOffsetsToTransaction() commits the supplied offsets as soon as the method returns.
cards.explanation: Offsets sent through sendOffsetsToTransaction() commit when their transaction commits.
cards.misconception: Returning from sendOffsetsToTransaction() completes the offset commit.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer begins and commits transactions in a consume-process-produce application.
cards.explanation: KafkaProducer owns the transaction API.
cards.misconception: The consumer manages the transaction for a consume-process-produce loop.

cards.statement: KafkaConsumer returns records from aborted transactions with its default isolation.level setting.
cards.explanation: read_uncommitted includes aborted transactional records.

source.title: Kafka 4.3 Consumer and Share Consumer Configs

cards.statement: With isolation.level=read_committed, KafkaConsumer can read past open transactions to the high watermark.
cards.explanation: read_committed consumers stop at the last stable offset while a transaction remains open.
cards.misconception: A read_committed consumer follows the high watermark through open transactions.

source.title: Kafka 4.3 Consumer and Share Consumer Configs

cards.statement: The Kafka docs recommend enable.auto.commit=true for transactional consume-process-produce applications.
cards.explanation: Use enable.auto.commit=false for transactional offset updates.
cards.misconception: Automatic offset commits fit transactional consume-process-produce processing.

cards.statement: Exactly-once output to an external system depends on that system's cooperation with the application.
cards.explanation: Kafka transactions alone do not coordinate external writes.

cards.statement: With the same transactional.id, initTransactions() aborts a failed producer's transaction left open before commit.
cards.explanation: KafkaProducer resolves a previous transaction for the same transactional.id during initialization. It waits if commit has already started.

cards.statement: Kafka caps a transaction.timeout.ms above transaction.max.timeout.ms at the broker's configured maximum.
cards.explanation: Kafka rejects a requested transaction timeout above the broker maximum.
cards.misconception: Kafka silently clamps an excessive transaction timeout.

cards.statement: Since Kafka 4.0, Kafka advances a transactional producer's epoch for successive transactions.
cards.explanation: New epochs keep late writes out of subsequent transactions.

cards.statement: KafkaProducer.abortTransaction() can automatically rewind KafkaConsumer to the aborted transaction's input records.
cards.explanation: After a transaction abort, the application resets consumer position explicitly.
cards.misconception: Aborting a producer transaction also restores the consumer's current position.
